reviews.title: Save your time and $
reviews.text:
So, I joined 3 or 4 days ago. I had a few matches pressuring to communicate via other apps, so for fun I decided to reverse image search some of my matches. Imagine my shock and surprise, when I found the images were stolen from someone on insta. The actually person happened to be gay, recently married of his partner of 3 years, and live in Zurich. Coincidentally, Upward emailed stating “look at these matches” and that profile was one of the people featured only his location was the capital of Ethiopia, even though on app and per the scammer he was from Italy but was living in Ca. 

In fact, of the 15 people I matched with, 10 were scammers. I easily found the pictures that were stolen from profiles on Instagram that did not belong to the person on the app. I thought if the person was verified that it may help eliminate face profiles; I was wrong about that too. 

lol, 2 different profiles on upward (Frank and Adam) had both stollen picture from the same insta profile of someone from Malaga, Spain. Although,  Frank said he was from Italy and Adam said Cardiff. 

Additionally, I’ve had people match with me and the app will say they are 20+ miles away but they list where they live in their bio and some are 400-600 miles away. So, the distance isn’t  trustworthy either. 

Honestly, don’t waste your money unless you are willing to reverse image search and verify info.

reviews.title: Scammer Galore
reviews.text:
Disappointing Experience – Not What a Christian Dating App Should Be

I signed up for Upward because it advertises itself as a Christian dating app. I genuinely believed I would be connecting with like-minded Christians who walk with Christ, share biblical values, and are seeking meaningful, faith-centered relationships. Unfortunately, my experience has been the complete opposite.

The app is marketed toward Christians, yet I have encountered people from various religious backgrounds, including individuals who openly identify as atheists. While everyone is entitled to their beliefs, that defeats the purpose of advertising a dating platform specifically for Christians.

What is even more disturbing is the overwhelming number of suspicious profiles, dishonest individuals, and apparent scammers I have encountered. Instead of focusing on building genuine connections, I have spent an unreasonable amount of time trying to determine who is real, who is lying, and who may be attempting to scam someone.

The fact that people are paying for this experience makes it even more frustrating. When customers pay for a faith-based dating service, they should reasonably expect stronger safeguards, better screening, and a platform that reflects what it advertises.

In my experience, Upward’s vetting process appears seriously inadequate. A Christian dating app should be a place where people can pursue relationships rooted in faith, honesty, integrity, and shared values—not a place where users co

reviews.title: Punished for an honest mistake
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with Upward’s handling of my account.

My original account appeared to have a technical issue: despite actively using the app, I received no matches and repeatedly received the same “congratulations on sending your first like” notification. After seeking troubleshooting advice, I voluntarily deleted my account and created a replacement, not to evade a suspension or disciplinary action, but because I believed my original account was malfunctioning.

I had no prior disciplinary issues. When my replacement account was banned, I submitted a genuine appeal explaining what had happened and why I had acted as I did. My appeal was rejected, my account remains banned, and I received no specific explanation of what I supposedly did wrong beyond a generic reference to the Terms and Conditions or Community Guidelines.

I understand that platforms have rules, but users should be able to understand how those rules apply to their circumstances. A blanket rejection without a meaningful explanation is deeply frustrating, especially when the original issue appeared to be a technical problem.

I joined Upward hoping to meet someone who shared my Christian faith and serious intentions toward marriage. I found the experience on this app more promising than on other dating platforms, which makes this outcome particularly disappointing. I wish the company had offered clearer guidance, better transparency, and a more meaningful review of my appeal.

reviews.text:
This was the first dating app I decided to pay for thinking it was meant for finding Godly matches. Spiritual but not religious is an option on here. Which was flag #1.

4th- it recycles people you’ve already passed on. The database is small, which is uncontrollable on their part but if I’ve passed what would make me say yes 3 days later? 
I’ve only seen 3 instantly recognizable bots but other than seems pretty real as far as real members are concerned. 

All in all, it’s a kk eh grab not aimed at finding you a real connection. Real connections lead to you not needing the app, which hurts their bottom line. After the membership I won’t be back.

reviews.title: It’s Alright
reviews.text:
I’ve met some people solid Christians on this app, even if most of that are fairly distant from me geographically speaking. However, there’s a couple of key annoyances. First, the number of people who have already liked me never drops, and I can (and have) swiped in excess of 400 people on one sitting. Still 99+. Second (and this combines with the first one), it will repeatedly (and randomly) revert to my general geographic area, showing me the same faces I have seen countless times. If I swiped away on someone, I generally did that with intent. I don’t want to have to swipe past everyone again, and again, and again so that I can finally encounter those people who purportedly already liked me. Finally, excessive notifications (“WWJD? Prolly start swiping for singles” - yeah ... probably not. Ditch that notification). I appreciate it for what it is. Technically speaking, I’m not very impressed. Subscriptions are overly expensive, and (unlike Hinge) undos are behind a paywall. Could be worse, but could certainly be better. Edit: I bit the bullet and got a subscription, just to confirm my suspicions. The majority of the people who had already “liked” me were people that I recognized as having swiped away. App is poorly developed.

Edit: advertisements for alcohol now.

Edit: this app continues to get worse. Constantly pushing all the other Match Corp. dating apps on me. No, I don’t want a Tinder accounts.

I’m very disappointed with the customer support. I contacted them because I’m having trouble accessing my account, and I still haven’t received a response. At this point, I don’t even know if my account is still active, which is concerning because I can’t access it to check my information or delete the account if I choose to.

A dating app should provide timely support, especially when someone is unable to access their own account. I hope they improve their customer service and respond to users who are experiencing account issues.

Nothing I did would let me sign back in, and I only used my phone number for signing up, and had no way of accessing my account or subscription, so they basically barred me. I felt incredibly uncomfortable that I was locked out and had no control anymore over my personal information, subscription, or account. It took over a week of getting the situation fixed, in which I wanted them to completely delete my account. They would not give me a refund because I had already sent messages on my account (which doesn’t apply at all to what the subscription does btw), and claimed that I must’ve been “banned” without giving me any reasons when I had done absolutely nothing wrong at all. I barely talked to a couple of people and there was nothing wrong at all with our casual conversations. Communication from their support was inconsistent and poor. What a joke of a company, this is not at all a Christian company, and shouldn’t be used for Christian dating.

reviews.title: Owned by Tinder…Same Swipe Algorithm
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, a bunch of subpar looking women who get a match 40% of the time, while men receive a match 2% of the time (actual data).  Men outnumber women on swipe-apps more than 2:1.  The “Christian” wrapper doesn’t change the modern phenomenon we’re seeing in dating.  Recent polls show that women rate ~80% of men as being below average in looks.  This leaves the top ~20% of men receiving 98% of the matches.  Meanwhile, the “…Where are all of the good men?!” mystery remains alive and well inside of the female community.  Even if you manage to match with a woman, odds show that it falls on the man to impress that woman, but the woman relies on her looks/body to impress, not their character.  The ROI isn’t worth it.  Swipe-apps have created an unrealistic bubble of entitlement and self-justified promiscuity amongst women.  The wildly imbalanced amount of matches for females leaves them wondering why they’re liked so much, but no one wants to marry them.  The sad truth is that they’re choosing the men who want to rent the room, not move in. 

Understand that this is coming from a purely analytical perspective, not a “…I’m bitter I’m not getting enough matches to maintain my ego.” ideology.  All of my figures are data-backed and not intended to insult or anger anyone.  Completely fine if you disagree, and no judgement intended to be against anyone in specific.

Just like the good men are out there, so are the good women.  We’ve all just been led to believe that apps are the an

reviews.title: No distance filter kills it
reviews.text: The app itself seems to work fairly well overall, but the distance filter only being a suggestion makes this app useless to me. At first you’ll see mostly local profiles, but as you go through those you’ll see profiles at greater and greater distances, regardless of the filter you set. Within one day it got to the point I would have to go through 20 profiles that are 300+ miles away to see just one that’s 100 or less, which is a huge waste of time. If you’re okay with long distance this may be a great option, I see a decent number of positive reviews saying they found their spouse and I’m happy it worked for them, but if you’re not interested in long distance and don’t live near a large city you can likely be done with this app in one day like I was. I see reviews that are FOUR YEARS OLD complaining about the distance filter, with developer responses saying they were working on it. Clearly that was not true and they have no intention of making the distance filter work, every other dating app has figured that out by now. Also this is owned by the same conglomerate as Hinge and Tinder, so that should tell you how interested they are in helping you find a match.
